laws.rule: In Travemünde (Lübeck), overnight visitors pay a spa levy (Kurabgabe) per person per day: EUR 3.50 from 15 May to 14 September (about A$5.56, RBA rate of 30 October 2026) and EUR 2 the rest of the year; it includes the beach fee. Lübeck's old town and other districts charge no overnight tax.

laws.rule: Schleswig-Holstein Wadden Sea National Park (national park law of 17 December 1999): the park has two protection zones, and Zone 1 holds a no-use area. Under section 5, putting up tents or other movable shelters, storing things, and parking camper vans to sleep are prohibited; dogs must not run off the lead; driving any vehicle or bike on the land and mudflats, and riding horses without permission, are prohibited. In Zone 1, walking on the near-shore mudflats along the mainland coast and around the islands and the Halligen Oland, Langeness, Gröde, Hooge and Nordstrandischmoor, including for bathing, is allowed in areas the park authority approves with the councils; mudflat-walking routes are set separately. The park says walking on the mudflats on your own near the coast is allowed, and that you should check tide times for safety. Horse riding is allowed only in certain beach areas of St Peter-Ording (a badge is required) and a few other places.

Gesetz uber Sonn- und Feiertage (SFTG) section 5, section 6 and section 9
laws.rule: Schleswig-Holstein bans public events that do not suit the serious character of the day on Volkstrauertag and Totensonntag from 6 am to 8 pm, and on Good Friday from 2 am to 2 am the next day; public meetings and parades not tied to a church service are also banned then (section 6(1)). On Buss- und Bettag acts that disturb a church service are banned (section 6(2)). On Sundays and public holidays (except 1 May and 3 October) acts that disturb a church service are banned (section 5). A breach can be fined up to EUR 5,000 (about A$7,946) (section 9(2)). AUD at A$1 = EUR 0.6293 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026).

laws.heading: Gesetz zum Schutz vor den Gefahren des Passivrauchens section 2 and section 5
laws.rule: Schleswig-Holstein bans smoking tobacco products, including e-cigarettes, heated tobacco and vaporisers, in enclosed rooms of public offices and courts, hospitals, care homes, schools, childcare and youth facilities, adult education, universities, sports facilities, culture venues and bars and restaurants (section 2(1)). A breach can be fined up to EUR 1,000 (about A$1,589) (section 5(2)). AUD at A$1 = EUR 0.6293 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026).

laws.heading: Landeswaldgesetz (LWaldG) section 17, section 23 and section 38
laws.rule: In Schleswig-Holstein forests, driving or parking vehicles and caravans, camping in a tent, and bringing tame animals other than dogs on a lead onto forest paths need the forest owner's consent (section 17). Fire and smoking rules for the forest are set by ordinance of the forest ministry under section 23(3), which lets it limit fire and light and ban smoking in whole or part. Fines under section 38: up to EUR 100,000 (about A$158,900) for the gravest listed offences and up to EUR 10,000 (about A$15,890) for offences such as breaching the entry rules. AUD at A$1 = EUR 0.6293 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026).
laws.penalty_signal: Up to EUR 10,000; up to EUR 100,000 for the gravest offences.
